explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. Jesus says, "If you continue in My word, you are truly My disciples." Notice the word "continue." He's talking about sticking with it, not just showing up once. A recipe only works if you keep following it, and I've learned that the hard way.

Good guess, because the crowd leans on Abraham hard in a minute. But Jesus doesn't point to family at all here. He says, "If you continue in My word, you are truly My disciples." Being a disciple comes from staying in His word, not from who your ancestors were.

Jesus is teaching in the temple, so I see why it came to mind. But He never mentions giving here. He says, "If you continue in My word, you are truly My disciples." It's about staying with what He says.

Yes, "We have never been slaves to anyone." Now, friend, I'll just say it. Israel had a long history in Egypt, and God brought them out of it (Exodus 20:2). Jesus doesn't argue about that, though. He's headed somewhere deeper.

Close in sound, but that's not their word. They say, "We have never been slaves to anyone." They're pushing back on Jesus's talk of being set free. In their minds, you can't free someone who was never held.
Not quite, baker. Their words are, "We have never been slaves to anyone." They're asking why Jesus would talk about freedom when, to them, nobody ever had power over them. The answer is slaves.
That's right. Jesus says, "…everyone who sins is a slave to sin." Everyone. No exceptions listed, no family-tree discount. That's the slavery the crowd hadn't noticed.

I see the thinking, but Jesus draws no line like that. He says, "…everyone who sins is a slave to sin." He's speaking to people who said, "We are Abraham’s descendants…" and He puts them right in that "everyone." It's about sin, not about where you're from.

Bills are something plenty of people carry, friend. But Jesus isn't talking about that kind of owing here. He says, "…everyone who sins is a slave to sin." His point is about sin holding people, not money.
Almost, but look again at what Jesus says. "A slave does not remain in the house forever, but a son remains forever." Only one of the two stays. The slave doesn't, and the son does.

Right, baker. Jesus says, "A slave does not remain in the house forever, but a son remains forever." Two people live in that house, and only the son has a place there for good. Then Jesus says who can set people free.

Yes! "So if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed." Remember the picture of the son who remains in the house forever. Jesus is pointing to Himself. And "free indeed" means the real thing, not a sticker on the box saying free.

Good thought, since they're standing in the temple. But Jesus says, "…if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed." Remember the picture He just painted of a son in the house. The Son is the one who sets people free.
I get why you'd pick it, friend. But Jesus says, "…if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed." He circles back to the son in His house picture. The one who frees is the Son.

explanations.answer: His word has no place in them
explanations.explanation: That's the one. Jesus says they are trying to kill Him "…because My word has no place within you." He doesn't say they lack a family or a name. His word just has no room in them.

That does come up in other places (Mark 2:16), but not in this passage. Here Jesus says they are trying to kill Him "…because My word has no place within you." That's the reason He gives, and He gives only that one.
They're standing in the temple, so I see the connection. But Jesus doesn't say that here. He says they are trying to kill Him "…because My word has no place within you."

Not this time, baker. Jesus says the opposite. After mentioning their plan to kill Him, a man who told them the truth from God, He says, "Abraham never did such a thing." Abraham is the contrast, not the match.

Right. Jesus says they're trying to kill Him, a man who told them the truth He heard from God, and then adds, "Abraham never did such a thing." So Abraham is the example they're not following. That's why Jesus says they'd do Abraham's works if they were his children.
Yes, baker. They declare, "Our only Father is God Himself." Earlier they had said, "Abraham is our father…" Jesus answers that claim right away.
Moses, the leader God sent to bring Israel out of Egypt (Exodus 3:10), is a fair guess for this crowd. But he's not who they name here. They say, "Our only Father is God Himself."
David, Israel's famous king (2 Samuel 5:3), is a good guess. But they don't name him. They say, "Our only Father is God Himself." Before that, they had only named Abraham.

Yes. Jesus says, "If God were your Father, you would love Me, for I have come here from God." It's a test of the claim they just made. Jesus says that if God is their Father, they'd love the One He sent.
Not quite, friend. Doubt is what the crowd is already doing. Jesus says, "If God were your Father, you would love Me…" That's the word.
I can see why, with the mood in that temple. But Jesus says, "If God were your Father, you would love Me, for I have come here from God." It's love, and He says God sent Him.

Right, baker. Jesus says, "You belong to your father, the devil…" He also says the devil was "…a murderer from the beginning…" and "…the father of lies." That fits the other father Jesus mentioned earlier.

Herod, the king in Judea when Jesus was born (Matthew 2:1), is a fair guess. But Jesus names someone else. He says, "You belong to your father, the devil…" He's the murderer from the beginning and the father of lies.
Pharaoh, the king of Egypt who oppressed Israel (Exodus 1:11), is a fair guess. But Jesus names someone else. He says, "You belong to your father, the devil…" the father of lies.
Yes. Jesus says, "But because I speak the truth, you do not believe Me!" Sounds backwards, doesn't it? Truth is exactly what they're not taking in. I think that makes it a pretty heavy moment.
Careful, baker. Jesus says, "But because I speak the truth, you do not believe Me!" So the statement is true. That's the reason He gives.

explanations.answer: They do not belong to God
explanations.explanation: That's the reason Jesus gives. He says, "Whoever belongs to God hears the words of God. The reason you do not hear is that you do not belong to God." He doesn't point to schooling or other teachers. It's about whose they are.

explanations.answer: They were never taught the Law
explanations.explanation: It's a natural guess, but Jesus never says that. He says, "The reason you do not hear is that you do not belong to God." That's the reason He gives.

Reasonable, friend, but Jesus never says that. He says, "Whoever belongs to God hears the words of God. The reason you do not hear is that you do not belong to God." He doesn't mention other teachers.

Yes. They ask, "Are we not right to say that You are a Samaritan and You have a demon?" Samaritan is the first thing they call Him, and the demon comes second. Jesus answers the demon part right away.
I see the guess, baker, but that's not what they say here. Their words are, "…You are a Samaritan and You have a demon?" Neither Galilean nor training comes up in their question.

explanations.answer: A Nazarene who breaks the Law
explanations.explanation: That sounds like something this crowd might say, baker. But the verse says otherwise. They ask if they're right to say, "…You are a Samaritan and You have a demon?"
Yes. Jesus says, "I do not have a demon, but I honor My Father, and you dishonor Me." Notice He answers the insult by pointing to His Father. That's where His focus stays.
Not quite, baker. Jesus says, "I do not have a demon, but I honor My Father, and you dishonor Me." The word is honor.
Not that one, friend. Jesus says, "I do not have a demon, but I honor My Father…" He doesn't avoid the Father at all. He says the crowd is the one who dishonors Him.
Yes. They declare, "Now we know that You have a demon!" They'd already said it once, and this time they say they know it. Jesus's promise about never seeing death is what set them off.
I see why you'd hesitate, but the verse says otherwise. After Jesus says anyone who keeps His word will never see death, they declare, "Now we know that You have a demon!" So it's true.
Yes. They ask, "Are You greater than our father Abraham?" They point out that Abraham died, and so did the prophets. Then they ask, "Who do You claim to be?"
Good guess, friend, but not their word. They ask, "Are You greater than our father Abraham?" They're asking if Jesus is above Abraham.
Not richer, friend. They ask, "Are You greater than our father Abraham?" Nobody brings up money here. It's about greatness, not wealth.
Yes. Jesus says, "If I said I did not know Him, I would be a liar like you." Then He adds, "But I do know Him, and I keep His word." He says it plainly.
Look again, baker. Jesus says, "If I said I did not know Him, I would be a liar like you." So it's true. He does know the Father, and He says so.
Not quite. Jesus says the opposite about Abraham. He says, "Your father Abraham rejoiced that he would see My day. He saw it and was glad." So Abraham did see it.
Right. Jesus says, "Your father Abraham rejoiced that he would see My day. He saw it and was glad." Abraham is the very man the crowd keeps pointing to. Jesus says he was glad about His day.

Yes, baker, it's stones. The verse says, "…they picked up stones to throw at Him." It's a heavy ending to the argument, and I think it's worth slowing down for. It comes right after Jesus says, "before Abraham was born, I am!"
Close in feel, baker, but not what the verse says. It says, "…they picked up stones to throw at Him." Stones, not dust. That's their response to what Jesus just said about Abraham.
Not torches, friend. The verse says, "…they picked up stones to throw at Him." It's stones. Torches aren't in the verse.

explanations.answer: He was hidden and went out
explanations.explanation: That's what the verse says. "…Jesus was hidden and went out of the temple area." John doesn't say how He was hidden, so I won't guess either. The text gives only that He was hidden and went out.
Good guess, but the verse doesn't say that. It says, "…Jesus was hidden and went out of the temple area." No one is named as leading Him.
That would be a movie scene, friend. But the verse says, "…Jesus was hidden and went out of the temple area." No rooftops mentioned.
